answer: Every sign-up must carry a sequential-squaring proof whose input must mirror the hash of the previous registration. The ledger therefore admits identities strictly one at a time, and nobody can precompute. Validators reject any entry whose proof covers less than 12 seconds plus 0.4 seconds per identity ever registered, an all-time count that never resets. A faster crystal or a GPU rack cannot split the squaring, so planting a grove of fakes is serial: the 5,000th demands over 33 minutes.
